platforms.name: Unconjugated 2'-MOE phosphorothioate ASO, intrathecal lumbar bolus (Ionis/Biogen-class chemistry)
platforms.architecture: Naked single-strand ASO, 2'-O-methoxyethyl/PS backbone. Two payload modes both relevant here: RNase H1 gapmer (knockdown) and fully 2'-MOE steric-block splice switcher (the mode CDKL5 upregulation mechanisms require). No ligand; uptake is bulk CSF convection plus non-specific endocytosis.
platforms.reaches_cell: Yes for most required cells, unevenly. Cortex, cerebellar cortex, hippocampus, pons, medulla, thalamus, amygdala and spinal cord reach concentrations similar to spinal cord; deep nuclei (caudate/putamen) are >10-fold lower than cortex. Critically for CDD, single-cell profiling in NHP thalamus/caudate/putamen showed all neuronal subtypes knocked down as deep as or deeper than bulk tissue, with microglia deepest and endothelium weakest — so the deep-brain gap is an exposure gradient, not a neuron-exclusion problem. Retina and visual-pathway photoreceptors are NOT covered by intrathecal dosing and need a separate intravitreal arm. Heart/periphery get negligible exposure after IT (safety advantage, no cardiac liability).
platforms.functional_activity: Yes — productive nuclear and cytoplasmic activity in human neurons is established for both payload modes: approved RNase H (tofersen, zilganersen) and approved/late-stage steric-block splice switching (nusinersen; zorevunersen).
platforms.human_pd: Zilganersen (ION-373, GFAP): 25 or 50 mg IT q12w, 53 patients aged 2–53; plasma GFAP −33.6% (p=0.003), 10-m walk gait speed LSM difference +33.3% (p=0.041) at week 61; FDA-approved 3 Sep 2026 (Zanvastro). Diranersen/BIIB080 (MAPT): 60 or 115 mg IT; CSF total tau reduced ~50–60% from baseline across doses over 76 weeks. Tofersen: CSF SOD1 −37% at 100 mg vs no change on placebo (−1%/−27%/−21% at 20/40/60 mg) — a dose-response worth noting because it shows naked IT ASO target engagement can be modest even in the best-exposed tissue (spinal motor neurons). Zorevunersen (TANGO splice-switch upregulation, Dravet children): clinical and safety data exist but no public human molecular PD (no human SCN1A/Nav1.1 measurement) — so there is NO human PD number anywhere for an upregulation ASO.
platforms.dose_frequency: Pediatric precedent is strong: nusinersen 12 mg IT ×4 loading then q4 months from newborn; zilganersen 25–50 mg q12 weeks, label extended below age 2 by PK modelling; zorevunersen 70 mg (day 1, wk 8) then 45 mg (wk 24, wk 40) in children 2–<18. Plan on q8–16-week lumbar punctures under sedation for a CDD infant/child population.
platforms.toxicity: Manageable and characterised in children: vomiting, back pain, headache, post-lumbar-puncture syndrome, and aseptic meningitis (zilganersen label warning). Communicating hydrocephalus requiring VP shunt reported post-marketing with nusinersen. Preclinical hazard to design against: PS-ASO macrovesicular vacuolation of hippocampal neurons in NHP — directly relevant since hippocampus is a required CDD tissue. Sequence-dependent neurotoxicity screening is mandatory.
platforms.access: Fully buildable in-house. Chemistry is generic/off-patent-adjacent, CROs synthesise GMP MOE-PS, and the n-of-1/individualised ASO regulatory path (FDA individualised-ASO guidance) plus academic IT dosing infrastructure exist. No licence needed for the delivery route. This is the default for a first CDD program.

findings.claim: In NHP thalamus, caudate and putamen all neuronal subtypes showed Malat1 knockdown similar to or deeper than bulk tissue after intrathecal ASO.
Intrathecal ASO exposure is high in cortex/spinal cord/periventricular regions and >10-fold lower in deep brain nuclei such as striatum.
Zilganersen 25/50 mg IT q12w in 53 AxD patients aged 2–53: gait speed LSM difference 33.3% (p=0.041), plasma GFAP −33.6% (p=0.003).
Zilganersen approved 3 Sep 2026 as first Alexander disease treatment, intrathecal every 3 months; AEs include post-LP syndrome and aseptic meningitis.
Diranersen (BIIB080) Phase 2 CELIA: 60 or 115 mg IT q12–24w reduced CSF total tau by roughly 50–60%; advancing to registrational development.
Tofersen CSF SOD1 reduction was 37% at 100 mg versus 1%, 27% and 21% at 20, 40 and 60 mg.
Zorevunersen Phase 3 EMPEROR: children 2–<18, 70 mg IT at day 1 and week 8 then 45 mg at weeks 24 and 40; 162 enrolled, readout Q3 2027.
Nusinersen: 12 mg intrathecal, 4 loading doses then every 4 months; post-marketing communicating hydrocephalus, some needing VP shunt.
PS-ASO-related macrovesicular vacuolation of hippocampal neurons documented in nonhuman primates.

platforms.name: TfR1 antibody/Fab–oligonucleotide conjugates, intravenous (Denali OTV; Dyne FORCE; Avidity AOC)
platforms.architecture: Anti-human-TfR1 antibody or Fab covalently linked to an oligonucleotide payload (Denali OTV: maleimide-C6 linker at engineered Ser239 of a TfR antibody; Dyne FORCE: Fab-ASO; Avidity AOC: mAb-siRNA or mAb-PMO). Receptor-mediated transcytosis across brain endothelium, then receptor-mediated uptake by parenchymal cells.
platforms.reaches_cell: Preclinically yes, and more uniformly than intrathecal naked ASO. Systemic OTV in human-TfR1 knock-in mice gave sustained Malat1 knockdown across multiple CNS regions and in endothelial cells, neurons, astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes, with more uniform biodistribution than naked ASO; robust activity also in cynomolgus macaques. Dyne reported FORCE Fab-ASO CNS delivery in mice and NHP with broader brain distribution than intrathecal unconjugated ASO. Caveat for CDD: OTV also knocked down target in quadriceps and cardiac muscle — i.e. heart is exposed, which is a new safety surface an IT ASO does not have, and TfR1 is on erythroid precursors (reticulocyte/anaemia risk requires engineered monovalent, affinity-tuned binding).
platforms.functional_activity: Yes in animals for RNase H payloads. For the payload CDD actually needs (steric-block splice switching), the receptor-conjugate precedent is Avidity's AOC 1044, a TfR1 mAb–PMO that produced exon-44 skipping and dystrophin increases in DMD patients — proof that a TfR1 conjugate can deliver functional splice-switching chemistry to human cells, but in muscle, not brain.
platforms.human_pd: No human CNS PD yet. DNL628 (OTV:MAPT) dosed its first Phase 1b patient in March 2026; initial CSF tau/p-tau biomarker data guided to 1H 2027. Human PD for TfR1 conjugates exists only in muscle disease (Avidity/Dyne DM1, DMD, FSHD programs). Treat brain exposure in humans as unproven as of today.
platforms.dose_frequency: IV infusion, anticipated monthly to quarterly based on OTV preclinical durability and the Phase 1b design (adverse events assessed over 37 weeks). Avoids repeated lumbar punctures — a real advantage in a severely disabled paediatric population.
platforms.toxicity: Known class risks: TfR1-mediated reticulocyte depletion/anaemia, infusion reactions, immunogenicity against the antibody, and on-target activity in heart and skeletal muscle. Paediatric exposure data: none. Repeat IV dosing in infants with a BBB-crossing antibody is unprecedented.
platforms.access: Not buildable in-house in any realistic timeframe. OTV is Denali-proprietary and clinically unpartnered for rare paediatric CNS upregulation; FORCE is Dyne-proprietary; AOC is Avidity-proprietary. Route is partnering/licensing only, and all three are prioritising large indications. Realistic posture: keep as a second-generation delivery upgrade and open business-development conversations now, but do not make the CDD program contingent on it.

findings.claim: OTV (TfR1 antibody–ASO) given IV produced sustained Malat1 knockdown across mouse CNS regions and in neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes and endothelium, plus quadriceps and cardiac muscle; robust activity in macaques.
First patient dosed in Phase 1b of DNL628 (OTV:MAPT) in March 2026; initial CSF biomarker data expected 1H 2027.
Dyne FORCE Fab-ASO achieved CNS delivery via TfR1 in mice and NHP, with broader brain distribution than intrathecal unconjugated ASO.
TfR1-targeted AOCs include siRNA and PMO payloads; AOC 1044 (DMD exon 44 PMO) has shown dystrophin increases clinically.

platforms.name: Peptide–oligonucleotide conjugates for systemic CNS delivery (LDLR/ApoB11, ApoE-derived BPP)
platforms.architecture: Short receptor-binding or BBB-penetrating peptide conjugated to an ASO or PMO. ApoB11 binds LDL receptor; ApoE-derived BPP peptides exploit lipoprotein-receptor transcytosis. Payload can be steric-block PMO, which is mechanism-compatible with CDKL5 upregulation.
platforms.reaches_cell: Preclinical rodent brain and spinal cord only. ApoB11-ASO given systemically crossed the BBB with sustained CNS retention; BPP-PMO reached brain and spinal cord of SMN2 transgenic mice. No cell-type-resolved neuronal coverage in primates. Peripheral tissue exposure (liver, kidney) is high; cardiac data not retrieved.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes but weak. Systemic ApoB11-ASO gave ~50% α-synuclein knockdown in transgenic mice. The only upregulation-relevant datapoint is BPP8-PMO raising full-length SMN2 in mouse brain ~1.25-fold — a small effect, and below what a CDKL5 program would need from a bounded-window standpoint it may actually be in range, but it is not primate-validated.
platforms.human_pd: None found. Searched for peptide-conjugated oligonucleotide CNS clinical data; the clinically advanced peptide conjugates (PepGen-class EDO/CPP-PMO) are muscle programs and I retrieved no human CNS PD for any peptide-oligo conjugate.
platforms.dose_frequency: Undefined in humans. Rodent work uses repeated systemic (IV/SC) dosing; translational dose and interval unknown.
platforms.toxicity: Historical class liability is cationic/arginine-rich CPP nephrotoxicity and complement/infusion effects; the lipoprotein-receptor peptides above were reported tolerable in mice but there is no primate or human safety package.
platforms.access: Most open class commercially — several of these peptides are academic publications with licensable or freely implementable chemistry, so an internal build is feasible. But it is a discovery-stage delivery bet: a CDD program choosing this accepts 3–5 years of delivery derisking on top of payload discovery.

findings.claim: Systemically delivered ApoB11-conjugated ASO crossed the BBB, showed sustained CNS retention and ~50% α-synuclein reduction in a synucleinopathy mouse model.
ApoE-derived BBB-penetrating peptide-PMO conjugates given systemically increased full-length SMN2 in brain and spinal cord of transgenic mice; BPP8-PMO gave ~1.25-fold brain increase.
Review of CNS oligonucleotide bioconjugates covering peptide, antibody and lipid ligands.

platforms.name: Divalent/branched and lipid-conjugated siRNA, intrathecal (Alnylam mivelsiran; Atalanta di-siRNA) and subcutaneous RNAi (Arrowhead TRiM)
platforms.architecture: Chemically stabilised siRNA, either lipophilic-conjugated (mivelsiran, IT) or two siRNAs covalently branched (di-siRNA, IT), or Arrowhead's TRiM constructs including a subcutaneous CNS-directed design. Payload is RNAi — Argonaute-dependent, cytoplasmic, degradative.
platforms.reaches_cell: Yes, and this class has the best-documented deep-brain reach of any clinical CNS oligo platform; di-siRNA is explicitly positioned for historically inaccessible deep structures and showed ~6 months durability preclinically. Arrowhead's subcutaneous ARO-MAPT achieved 70–80% MAPT mRNA reduction across 12 NHP brain regions (up to 85% in cortex) after three weekly SC doses, which if replicated in humans would be the first non-invasive route to broad neuronal coverage.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes for knockdown. MECHANISM MISMATCH is the decisive point for CDKL5: RNAi cannot perform poison-exon suppression, intron-retention correction, uORF relief or 3'UTR masking — all nuclear or translational steric-block mechanisms. The only CDKL5 mechanism this platform could serve is degrading a repressive natural antisense transcript (antagoNAT-equivalent), and no CDKL5 NAT was retrievable.
platforms.human_pd: Strong, and the best human numbers in CNS oligonucleotides: mivelsiran (ALN-APP, IT) single dose lowered CSF sAPPβ by up to 90% within 2 weeks with >70% maintained ≥3 months, and 50/75 mg single doses remained ~30% below baseline at 1 year; multiple-dose peak CSF sAPPβ −84.5% at month 1, −61.1% sustained at month 10, with no CSF protein or WBC elevation. Atalanta ATL-101 is IND-stage with no human data. ARO-ATXN2 is in Phase 1/2a; ARO-MAPT human readout guided to 2H 2026.
platforms.dose_frequency: Mivelsiran: intrathecal, dosing intervals of 6 months or longer are plausible given 1-year PD persistence. ARO-MAPT: subcutaneous, weekly loading then maintenance. Far fewer procedures than a q8–12-week ASO.
platforms.toxicity: Mivelsiran single-dose Phase 1: mild-to-moderate AEs, no CSF protein or pleocytosis signal. Class risks remain lumbar-puncture-related and sequence-dependent off-target; paediatric CNS siRNA experience is essentially nil.
platforms.access: Platform-proprietary (Alnylam, Atalanta, Arrowhead) — licensing only, and for CDD the licence would buy a modality that cannot execute the required mechanism. Correct use of this evidence: it sets the bar for how much CNS exposure and durability are achievable, and it supports a di-siRNA-style architecture only if CDD strategy shifts to NAT degradation or to a downstream knockdown target.

findings.claim: Mivelsiran single IT dose lowered CSF sAPPα/sAPPβ up to 90% within 2 weeks with >70% reduction maintained ≥3 months; no CSF protein or WBC elevation in 20 patients.
Multiple-dose mivelsiran: peak CSF sAPPβ change −84.5% at month 1, largely sustained at −61.1% through month 10.
Atalanta di-siRNA reaches deep brain regions with potent, ~6-month-durable knockdown preclinically; ATL-101 is IT-delivered and IND-stage.
ARO-MAPT achieved 70–80% MAPT mRNA reduction across 12 NHP brain regions (up to 85% cortical) after three weekly subcutaneous doses; human data 2H 2026.

platforms.name: Intravitreal unconjugated ASO (retina and visual-pathway arm)
platforms.architecture: Naked steric-block or RNase H ASO injected into the vitreous; retinal cells take it up without a ligand. Required as a separate arm because the CDD tissue list includes retina and visual-pathway neurons, which intrathecal dosing does not reach.
platforms.reaches_cell: Yes — photoreceptors and inner retina. Sepofarsen reached foveal cone photoreceptors in CEP290-LCA10 patients. For the upregulation mechanism specifically, STK-002 (an OPA1 non-productive-exon ASO, the closest payload analogue to a CDKL5 TANGO ASO) increased OPA1 protein in retinal tissue of cynomolgus monkeys and rabbits at 4 weeks, persisting to 8 weeks in monkeys.
platforms.functional_activity: Yes, including functional upregulation: STK-002 dose-dependently increased OPA1 protein in human cells including ADOA patient fibroblasts and improved mitochondrial function.
platforms.human_pd: Sepofarsen Phase 1b/2: visual function and retinal structure peaked near 3 months post-injection with efficacy sustained at 15 months; durable single-injection improvement replicated in individual patients. STK-002 first patient dosed in Phase 1 in February 2026 — no human PD yet.
platforms.dose_frequency: Single or infrequent intravitreal injection; sepofarsen's durability (months to >1 year per injection) suggests 6–12-month intervals.
platforms.toxicity: Dose-dependent ocular AEs with sepofarsen (cataract, inflammation) but a manageable profile. Intravitreal injection in a child with CDD requires general anaesthesia, which must be weighed against the clinical weight of the visual phenotype.
platforms.access: Fully buildable in-house; same chemistry and manufacturing as the IT arm, only a different administration route. Low incremental cost once a lead CDKL5 upregulation ASO exists.

findings.claim: Intravitreal sepofarsen in LCA10 showed manageable safety with dose-dependent ocular AEs; visual function and retinal structure peaked ~3 months post-injection with sustained efficacy at 15 months.
STK-002, an ASO blocking a non-productive OPA1 exon, increased OPA1 protein in human cells and in monkey and rabbit retina at 4 weeks, persisting to 8 weeks in monkeys.
Stoke dosed the first patient in a Phase 1 study of STK-002 for autosomal dominant optic atrophy in February 2026.

platforms.name: Xist-directed X-reactivation (ASO plus DNMT inhibitor combination)
platforms.architecture: Nuclear-acting ASO against XIST or Xist-interactome factors, combined with a small-molecule DNA methyltransferase inhibitor. Delivery vehicle would be a standard IT ASO plus a systemic small molecule — i.e. no new delivery technology is needed, which is why it is worth listing here.
platforms.reaches_cell: Delivery-wise yes: the ASO component uses the validated IT route with neuronal coverage described above. The limitation is biological, not delivery — reactivation must occur in the specific neurons that silenced the wild-type allele, and the DNMT inhibitor must reach the same neurons at a tolerated dose.
platforms.functional_activity: Demonstrated in vitro and in mice for MECP2: an Xist ASO plus 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine achieved up to 30,000-fold MECP2 upregulation from the inactive X in cultured cells, and brain-specific genetic Xist ablation plus short-term Aza modelled the synergy in vivo without evident toxicity; the inactive X was selectively reactivated. The same paper explicitly names CDKL5 syndrome as a target disease.
platforms.human_pd: None. No clinical X-reactivation program retrieved.
platforms.dose_frequency: Undefined. Would pair repeat IT ASO (q8–16 weeks by analogy) with intermittent systemic DNMT inhibition — a chronic genotoxic/epigenetic exposure in children.
platforms.toxicity: The binding constraint. Genome-scale: de-repression of hundreds of X-linked genes, reactivation of the mutant allele in the other half of neurons, and paediatric chronic nucleoside DNMT-inhibitor exposure. Safety surface is far wider than any gene-specific ASO.
platforms.access: Buildable technically (ASO plus a marketed DNMT inhibitor) but not advisable as the lead. Keep as a mechanism-of-interest with an academic collaboration, not a development path.

findings.claim: Xist ASO plus a DNA methylation inhibitor achieved 30,000-fold MECP2 upregulation from the inactive X in cultured cells; brain-specific Xist ablation plus short-term Aza modelled synergy in vivo without evident toxicity, with selective Xi reactivation. CDKL5 syndrome is named as a target.

platforms.name: Intrathecal AAV9 gene replacement (non-oligo comparator that sets the efficacy bar)
platforms.architecture: AAV9 carrying a functional human CDKL5 cassette, delivered into CSF. Included because it is the only CDKL5-specific CNS delivery program in active development and it defines what the oligo program must beat or complement.
platforms.reaches_cell: Intrathecal AAV9 targets CNS broadly; CDD-specific preclinical work exists, including secretable cell-penetrating TATk-CDKL5 designs intended to cross-correct neighbouring neurons and so address the mosaic coverage problem that any mutation-agnostic approach faces.
platforms.functional_activity: Preclinical only: gene replacement improved phenotypes in Cdkl5 models, and a cross-correction approach improved pathology in CDD patient-derived cortical organoids and in mosaic Cdkl5 mice.
platforms.human_pd: None. UX055 is in preclinical development per Ultragenyx; no clinical CDKL5 gene therapy data retrieved.
platforms.toxicity: AAV class risks (immune response, dorsal root ganglion toxicity, hepatotoxicity) plus the CDKL5-specific overexpression liability — uncontrolled, permanent, non-titratable expression is exactly the wrong profile for a gene with a bounded upper safety limit.
platforms.access: Ultragenyx-proprietary. The strategic read for an ASO program: a titratable, reversible, dose-adjustable oligonucleotide that raises endogenous CDKL5 within a bounded window is differentiated against a one-shot non-titratable vector, and that argument depends on the ASO delivery platform being the conventional IT route whose dose can be adjusted.

findings.claim: UX055 is an AAV9 gene therapy for CDD delivered by injection into the CSF, in preclinical development.
A cross-correction gene therapy using secretable cell-penetrating TATk-CDKL5 improved pathology in CDD patient-derived cortical organoids.
Igk-TATk-CDKL5 gene therapy showed safety and efficacy in mosaic Cdkl5 deficiency models.

naked_baseline: Best unconjugated baseline is a fully 2'-MOE PS steric-block ASO given as an intrathecal lumbar bolus, with an intravitreal companion for the retinal arm. Dose and frequency, from approved/late-stage paediatric precedents: zilganersen 25 or 50 mg IT every 12 weeks (approved 3 Sep 2026, ages 2+ and extended below 2 by PK modelling); nusinersen 12 mg ×4 loading then every 4 months from newborn; zorevunersen — the closest payload analogue, a splice-switching upregulation ASO in children 2–<18 with a DEE — 70 mg at day 1 and week 8, then 45 mg at weeks 24 and 40. So plan 20–70 mg IT, q8–16 weeks, in children. Exposure numbers: CSF/target engagement of 37% (tofersen CSF SOD1, 100 mg) to ~50–60% (diranersen CSF tau) in well-perfused regions; cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus, brainstem and spinal cord are well covered, deep nuclei are >10-fold lower in drug concentration, but single-cell NHP data show all neuronal subtypes in thalamus/caudate/putamen are engaged as deeply as or more deeply than bulk tissue (PMID 40857674) — so required CDD neuron classes are reachable. Critical gap: there is no human molecular PD number for ANY upregulation ASO, so the CDKL5 fold-increase achievable in human neurons is unmeasured; the retina needs intravitreal (sepofarsen, STK-002 precedent), and no naked oligo reaches it from CSF.
payload_vs_delivery: Delivery to CDD neurons is largely solved by plain intrathecal ASO; the unknown is payload. The 37–90% numbers quoted above all come from knockdown of highly amenable targets and say nothing about CDKL5 upregulation magnitude. No CDKL5 poison exon, NAT or uORF was retrievable — including in a 2026 brain poison-exon atlas with no CDKL5 entry. Target amenability, not delivery, dominates risk; conjugate platforms are also mechanism-incompatible (RNAi) or inaccessible.
